title: Transport Systems Summary
content:
# Transport Systems Summary

## Learning Objectives
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Compare transport in animals and plants
- Link structure to function in transport systems
- Explain why different organisms have different transport needs
- Review key concepts from the transport topic

## Introduction

This lesson brings together the key concepts of transport in both animals and plants. Understanding how transport systems work, and why they differ between organisms, provides insight into how life has evolved to meet the challenge of moving substances around bodies.

## Key Concepts

### Why Transport Systems Exist

**The surface area to volume ratio problem:**

| Organism size | SA:V ratio | Diffusion alone? |
|--------------|------------|------------------|
| Small (single cell) | Large | Yes |
| Large (multicellular) | Small | No |

**Large organisms need transport systems because:**
- Diffusion too slow over large distances
- Cells deep inside cannot get resources
- Waste removal would be too slow
- Metabolic demands are high

### Comparing Animal and Plant Transport

| Feature | Animals | Plants |
|---------|---------|--------|
| Pump | Heart | None (passive/active loading) |
| Transport medium | Blood | Water (xylem) / sap (phloem) |
| O₂ transport | Haemoglobin in RBCs | Dissolved in water/air |
| Nutrient transport | In plasma | Sucrose in phloem |
| Circulation | Closed, circular | Open-ended (xylem) |
| Direction | Pumped both ways | Xylem up; phloem both ways |

### Human Circulatory System Summary

| Component | Function |
|-----------|----------|
| Heart | Pump blood around body |
| Arteries | Carry blood away from heart |
| Veins | Return blood to heart |
| Capillaries | Exchange with tissues |
| Blood | Transport medium |

**Double circulation:**
- Pulmonary: Heart → Lungs → Heart
- Systemic: Heart → Body → Heart

**Advantages:** High pressure, efficient delivery

### Blood Components Summary

| Component | Function |
|-----------|----------|
| Plasma | Transports dissolved substances |
| Red blood cells | Transport oxygen |
| White blood cells | Immune defence |
| Platelets | Blood clotting |

### Blood Vessels Summary

| Vessel | Walls | Lumen | Valves | Pressure |
|--------|-------|-------|--------|----------|
| Artery | Thick, elastic | Small | No | High |
| Vein | Thin | Large | Yes | Low |
| Capillary | 1 cell thick | Tiny | No | Very low |

### Plant Transport Summary

| Tissue | Transports | Direction | Mechanism | Cells |
|--------|------------|-----------|-----------|-------|
| Xylem | Water, minerals | Up | Transpiration pull | Dead |
| Phloem | Sugars | Source→Sink | Pressure flow | Living |

### Transpiration Stream

**Pathway:**
Soil → Root hair → Cortex → Xylem → Stem → Leaf veins → Mesophyll → Stomata → Air

**Driving force:** Transpiration pull (cohesion-tension)

**Factors affecting rate:**
- Light (increases)
- Temperature (increases)
- Humidity (decreases)
- Wind (increases)

### Translocation Summary

**Source to sink:**
- Sugars made in leaves (source)
- Transported to where needed (sink)
- Active loading requires ATP
- Can travel up or down

### Key Adaptations

| Structure | Adaptation | Function |
|-----------|------------|----------|
| Red blood cell | No nucleus, biconcave | More haemoglobin, large SA |
| Artery wall | Thick, elastic | Withstand pressure, smooth flow |
| Capillary wall | 1 cell thick | Exchange |
| Root hair | Long extension | Large SA for absorption |
| Xylem vessel | No end walls, lignified | Continuous water column |
| Sieve tube | Sieve plates, living | Allow flow while staying alive |

### Common Processes in Both Systems

| Process | In animals | In plants |
|---------|-----------|----------|
| Diffusion | Gas exchange in capillaries | Gas exchange in leaves |
| Osmosis | Tissue fluid formation | Water uptake in roots |
| Active transport | Some nutrient absorption | Mineral uptake, sugar loading |
| Mass flow | Blood circulation | Transpiration stream |

### Health and Disease

**Human cardiovascular problems:**
- Atherosclerosis (plaque build-up)
- Heart attack (blocked coronary artery)
- Stroke (blocked brain blood vessel)
- High blood pressure

**Prevention:**
- Healthy diet
- Regular exercise
- No smoking
- Manage stress

### Key Equations and Calculations

**Cardiac output:**
$$\text{Cardiac output} = \text{Heart rate} \times \text{Stroke volume}$$

**Transpiration rate:**
$$\text{Rate} = \frac{\text{Distance (or volume)}}{\text{Time}}$$

### Key Practicals

| Investigation | Method |
|--------------|--------|
| Effect of exercise on heart rate | Measure pulse before and after |
| Transpiration factors | Potometer with different conditions |
| Blood vessel structure | Microscopy of prepared slides |

### Linking Concepts

**Transport links to:**

| Topic | Connection |
|-------|------------|
| Cells | Cell structure, organelles for transport |
| Respiration | O₂ delivery, CO₂ removal |
| Nutrition | Nutrient transport |
| Excretion | Waste transport |
| Coordination | Hormone transport |
| Homeostasis | Heat distribution, glucose transport |

## Common Exam Questions

- Compare transport in plants and animals
- Explain why large organisms need transport systems
- Link structure to function in named transport structures
- Calculate cardiac output or transpiration rate

## Common Misconceptions Review

| Misconception | Reality |
|--------------|--------|
| Arteries carry oxygenated blood | Pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated |
| Xylem pumps water up | Water is pulled by transpiration |
| Plants only photosynthesize | Plants respire continuously |
| Blood is blue when deoxygenated | It's dark red; veins appear blue through skin |
| Phloem only carries sugars down | Phloem transports to wherever sinks are |

## Practice Questions

1. State one similarity and one difference between transport in animals and plants. (2 marks)

2. Explain why large multicellular organisms need transport systems. (3 marks)

3. Compare the structure of arteries and xylem vessels. (4 marks)

4. Calculate the cardiac output of a person with heart rate 72 bpm and stroke volume 70 mL. (2 marks)

5. Explain how red blood cells and xylem vessels are each adapted for transporting substances. (6 marks)

6. Discuss the similarities and differences between the transport systems of mammals and flowering plants. (6 marks)

## Key Terms Review

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Double circulation | Blood passes through heart twice per circuit |
| Transpiration | Water loss from leaves |
| Translocation | Sugar transport in phloem |
| Haemoglobin | Oxygen-carrying pigment |
| Cohesion | Water molecules attracting each other |
| Active loading | ATP-requiring loading of sucrose into phloem |

## Summary

- Large organisms need transport systems (diffusion too slow)
- Human circulatory system: heart, blood vessels, blood
- Double circulation maintains high pressure
- Blood transports oxygen, nutrients, waste, hormones
- Plant xylem: transports water up by transpiration pull
- Plant phloem: transports sugars by pressure flow
- Structures adapted to functions (thick walls for pressure, thin for exchange)
- Health maintained by lifestyle choices
- Transport links to all other body systems
